notes.meaning: People can think through their ideas and arrange their thoughts. Yet the right word at the right moment comes only from the Lord. We can make our plans, but God alone directs what is finally spoken and accomplished.

People easily talk themselves into believing that everything they do is pure and blameless. The Lord, however, looks straight into the heart and weighs our real motives. His judgment is the only one that truly matters.

The word commit carries the idea of rolling a heavy burden off your own back and onto God. When we give all our work and worries to Him, our thoughts become calm and steady. Our plans will succeed as they line up with His good will.

The Lord made the world so that everything serves His purpose and displays His glory. Even those who choose to live in rebellion do not escape His sovereign rule. Their path ends in just punishment on the day of trouble.

differ.view: God sovereignly ordained all things for His own glory, so that His justice is shown in the appointed destruction of the wicked.
God did not create anyone for destruction, but made humans free; when people choose evil and refuse to turn, He justly punishes them.

notes.meaning: The Lord detests proud hearts, even when people hide their pride behind polite manners. Proud sinners may join hands and support one another, but that will not keep them safe. God's judgment will certainly catch up with them.

Iniquity, or sin, is covered and forgiven through God's loving devotion and faithfulness in His covenant promises. A healthy, reverent fear of the Lord also gives believers the power to walk away from evil habits.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Personal sins can be atoned for and satisfied through human acts of mercy, charity, and giving to the poor.

notes.meaning: When a person's daily life brings pleasure to God, the Lord protects that person in special ways. God holds every human heart in His hands. He has the power to soften old hatreds and turn former enemies into peaceful neighbors.

Having modest means earned in an honest, godly way brings peace and a clean conscience. A huge income gained through fraud or injustice is actually a curse. Unjust wealth can never buy true happiness or God's blessing.

Human beings are given the ability to think ahead and chart out their course. Even so, the Lord is the One who directs each actual step and decides the final outcome. We should hold all our personal plans with humble trust in God.

A king acts as God's representative on earth when giving legal rulings. Because of this high calling, a ruler must never twist the truth or hand down unfair sentences. God expects kings and judges to govern with divine wisdom.

Fair dealings in daily business are not just human customs; they are established by God Himself. The Lord watches over market transactions and cares that merchants use honest stones and balances. Cheating a neighbor in trade violates God's own standard.

Godly rulers ought to detest evil behavior in themselves and in their people. A royal government does not last because of military power alone. A throne is made strong and secure only when it rests on righteousness and justice.

A good ruler welcomes counselors who speak the honest truth without flattery. Leaders are often surrounded by people who say only what sounds pleasing, but a wise king values advisors who offer upright words. Speaking candidly brings true honor to leadership.

In ancient times, a king's anger could mean immediate execution for the person who crossed him. His displeasure arrived like a messenger carrying a death sentence. A wise person uses calm, prudent words to soothe that anger before damage is done.

A ruler's warm, bright smile brings safety, comfort, and hope to his subjects. His royal favor is compared to spring rain clouds that water the fields right before harvest. That rain makes the difference between famine and plenty.

Seeking godly wisdom and understanding is far better than chasing piles of silver and gold. Wealth can buy material comfort, but only wisdom can heal the soul and bring eternal life. True insight is the greatest treasure anyone can gain.

Upright people travel along a well-marked road that turns away from sin and danger. Those who pay close attention to where their feet are going protect their own lives from disaster. Staying away from evil is the surest way to safety.

Arrogance leads people to believe they are untouchable and need no help from God or others. That kind of reckless overconfidence blinds a person to dangerous traps. A haughty, boastful spirit is always the warning sign that a terrible crash is coming.

It is much better to live quietly among humble people with little to your name than to share stolen riches with the proud. The proud will eventually meet destruction at God's hand. Humble believers may suffer now, but they enjoy peace with God.

Whoever listens carefully to God's word and manages life with discretion will find good things. Real, lasting happiness does not come from clever schemes, but from placing full trust in the Lord. Trusting God brings true peace of heart.

A person whose heart contains real wisdom will be recognized by others as sensible and discerning. When that person speaks with warmth and graciousness, the teaching becomes far easier to accept. Pleasant speech makes instruction welcome and fruitful.

Good understanding refreshes and protects a wise person like an unending spring of cool water. It brings health to the person and gives helpful guidance to neighbors. A fool, however, has nothing good to offer, and even his advice turns out to be foolishness.

A wise heart acts like a teacher to the mouth, thinking things through before words are spoken. Because the inner thoughts are rich with understanding, the person's speech carries real weight. Careful reflection makes a person's words far more convincing.

Gentle, uplifting words are like pure honey dripping from the comb. They bring sweet refreshment to a weary spirit and even bring health to the body. Kind words have real power to heal emotional wounds and restore strength.

A certain lifestyle or belief can seem completely reasonable and safe to a person's own mind. Human instincts, however, can be deeply mistaken without God's truth to guide them. What looks pleasant on the surface can lead straight to spiritual death.

A laborer's need for food drives him to get out and work every day. His own hunger acts as a helpful servant, pushing him forward so he does not fall into laziness. God built our physical appetites to encourage honest industry.

A worthless troublemaker works as hard to dig up dirt on others as a miner does searching for ore. Once he finds something harmful, his speech blazes like an uncontrolled fire. His words burn down reputations and cause immense pain.

A twisted person loves to spread arguments and stir up conflict wherever he goes. Even worse, someone who whispers private slander behind closed doors can poison trust. Gossip has the terrible power to tear apart even lifelong best friends.

A violent person is not content to do wrong alone; he tries to drag his neighbors along with him. He uses smooth promises to tempt innocent people into dangerous schemes. Walking with violent companions only leads toward a terrible end.

Little gestures like a sly wink or tight, pursed lips reveal what a schemer is thinking deep inside. He closes his eyes to focus his thoughts on how to pull off his evil plan. When someone acts this way, the harm is already halfway done in his heart.

Growing old is a blessing, and gray hair shines like an honorable crown when a person has walked with God. Long life is often God's reward for a life of obedience and wisdom. An elderly believer who has remained faithful deserves high honor and respect.

A person who is slow to anger shows greater strength than a mighty soldier. Winning a battle against an outside enemy is hard, but conquering one's own temper is far harder. Controlling your spirit is a much higher victory than taking a walled city.

People may cast lots into the fold of a robe to settle an uncertain question, but the result never comes by pure accident. The Lord oversees and directs every single outcome. Even the things that look like random chance are completely under God's control.
